clue.text: A return of pin money after spring vegetable peaks?

indicators.note: after places what precedes it second, behind the word that follows it

parts.note: taken as written
a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the words that follow are read from the end to the start

parts.note: a spit is the pin a roast turns on
sugar is slang for money

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about getting your spending money back once springtime is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The pin and the money are joined first and the pair is turned round together, then placed after A and the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: The tender pointed heads of the green spears are their tips, so the peaks of this spring crop are fairly described.

clue.text: See 13 Across
Strain in always uncoordinated movement

indicators.note: one word sits in the middle of another, enclosed on both sides by it

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always
to tax is to strain, as in taxing one's patience

explanation.surface: A medical note that constant stress leaves someone clumsy on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxy is the older medical name, a variant of ataxia, for loss of muscular control producing jerky clumsy motion.

clue.text: Old Mexican upset South Africa P.I.

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
tec is short for detective, and a P.I. is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A historical figure from Mexico is put out by a private eye from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people ruling central Mexico before the Spanish conquest, so a member of that ancient civilisation fits.

clue.text: Like supporters, won out of attrition after United lead

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so one thing is removed from the other
after places the earlier wordplay behind what follows it, so the closing words come first

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names
Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
attrition is a wearing down or away
W stands for won in a table of results

explanation.surface: A football report: after a United goal, the team's fans felt the victory came only through a war of attrition.
explanation.walkthrough: W for won is a results-table convention, and Pb is the chemical symbol; the clue's order is reversed, with 'after' sending the attrition part to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbearing means holding up or sustaining, which is exactly what supports and props do for whatever rests on them.

clue.text: The enemy marker, we hear, associates with rosemary and war?

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, so words that sound alike but are spelt differently are wanted

parts.note: thyme goes with rosemary, as in the song line parsley, sage, rosemary and thyme
peace is paired with war, as in Tolstoy's War and Peace

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what goes with a herb and with war, dressed up as a riddle about the foe.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is proverbially the enemy, so a clock or watch marks the enemy. The two herbs-and-novel partners are spoken aloud to give the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is often called the enemy, and a clock or watch is a device that marks and measures its passing.

clue.text: The shriek of the IT consultant?

definitions.text: The shriek of the IT consultant?

parts.note: surface reading: a scream of horror let out by a computer expert
setter's reading: shriek is printers' slang for the exclamation mark, and computer people have their own name for that symbol

explanation.surface: A computer expert screams on seeing the state of a client's system.
explanation.walkthrough: Both shriek and the answer are jargon names for the ! character; the answer is the one used in computing circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmers' slang calls the exclamation mark a pling, while typesetters call the same punctuation symbol a shriek.

clue.text: Summons the cat-o'-twenty-seven-tails?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a party's strictest written order to its MPs to attend and vote
second meaning, playful: a cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip with nine lashes, so three of them make twenty-seven

explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the whip's notice to MPs underlines a vote three times when attendance is compulsory; the question mark flags the jokey three-by-nine arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line whip is a strict instruction calling members of parliament to the chamber, effectively a summons to vote.

clue.text: It relaxes me somehow, the getting back from voyage

definitions.text: It relaxes me somehow, the getting back from voyage

indicators.note: relaxing loosens a set form, letting the letters fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of voyage

explanation.surface: A traveller says what eases them after a long journey is somehow coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay builds the phrase, and read straight it describes the comfort of arriving back from a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying expresses the relief and comfort of being in one's own house again after travelling.

clue.text: This is a surprise job to look after a kiln

parts.note: ho! is a cry of surprise

indicators.note: to look after is to take care of and keep safe, so one word holds another within it

parts.note: a post is a job or position
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is unexpectedly asked to mind a pottery kiln at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is a surprise' reads as a comment but stands for an exclamation. POST holds A, after HO.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a drying kiln, and one built for drying hops in Kent and similar regions takes this name.

clue.text: Italian kid, a fifty-something on a Vespa!

parts.note: a Bambi is a born-again middle-aged biker, someone of that age taking up motorbikes again
a Vespa is only a scooter, so the rider is not a real biker: no!

explanation.surface: A middle-aged person zipping round on an Italian scooter is treated as a child.
explanation.walkthrough: BAMBI is slang for a born-again middle-aged biker; the exclamation says a fifty-something on a mere scooter does not count.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is the Italian word for a little boy or baby, so it is literally an Italian child.

clue.text: Soon befitting the husband of a countess?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: before long, ahead of time

definitions.text: befitting the husband of a countess?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: a countess's husband is an earl, so -y makes an adjective for what suits him

explanation.surface: An etiquette question about what will shortly suit a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means in good time or sooner than expected, and a countess is married to an earl, hence the joke adjective.

clue.text: #1 song never a hit, keeping up with a track on a #1 album

definitions.text: #1 song never a hit, keeping up with a track on a #1 album

parts.note: surface reading: a paradox, a chart-topping song that was never a hit

parts.words: keeping up with a track on a #1 album
parts.note: setter's reading: a famous Oasis track from the chart-topping album (What's the Story) Morning Glory?, never itself released as a UK single, whose title is two words for top-quality things

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a song can be number one yet never a hit while sharing an album with chart-toppers.
explanation.walkthrough: The '#1' in front of 'song' describes the song's classy title rather than its chart place; the album it closes did reach number one.
explanation.definitionFit: This Oasis song closes their 1995 chart-topping album but was never issued as a British single, so it never charted.

clue.text: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder

definitions.text: is in the eye of the beholder
definitions.note: verb phrase; the answer as a verb means seems
definitions.meaning: second meaning: seems or appears, how something strikes whoever is watching

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb reads as one statement; split it after 'Beauty' and both halves define the same word, one a noun and one a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Good looks are physical attractiveness, and to look a certain way is how something appears to whoever sees it.

clue.text: Companion that a poker player shouldn't have in place …

indicators.note: one thing is put inside another, which wraps around it

parts.note: a site is a place or location
a tell is an unconscious giveaway of a poker hand, which a good player must avoid

explanation.surface: Advice on what a card player's partner ought not to give away at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a body orbiting a planet, or a dependent follower, both senses of an attendant that travels alongside something.

clue.text: Many equate reduced force with current, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong and fallen into disorder, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
force cut down to its abbreviation, F, as in physics
W is short for with
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A physics student gloomily notes that many people link a weakened force with electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an understated idiom for a considerable number, the same sense as a lot or numerous.

clue.text: … money put down, game up in the air …

parts.note: a quid is British slang for a pound
to ditch something is to drop or discard it

explanation.surface: Cash laid on a bet while the match itself is still undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in the air' looks like 'uncertain', but read literally it says the sport is played aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Harry Potter books this sport is played by witches and wizards flying on broomsticks high above the pitch.

clue.text: See 20 Across
Vixen finally going to ground narrowly avoided disaster

definitions.note: verb phrase; the answer is a noun for such an escape

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of vixen
a fox goes to earth when it hides in its burrow, so earthing is going to ground

explanation.surface: A hunted she-fox reaches her burrow at the last moment and escapes the hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, a situation in which catastrophe was only just averted.

clue.text: House inaccessible in their years in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left
in says the letters lie inside the following words, spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Elderly people living out their later years in a remote retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest on a high crag, and by extension any lofty dwelling hard to reach.

clue.text: This time for the mind-blowing rallies!

definitions.text: This time for the mind-blowing rallies!

indicators.note: rallying regroups scattered forces in fresh formation, so the letters reassemble

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An excited announcement that the season of spectacular tennis exchanges has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the clue describes the event itself; rallies are long exchanges of shots in tennis, so the anagram signal doubles as the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon is the London grass-court tennis championship, lasting two weeks each summer and famous for long rallies.

clue.text: … more of the same a weaver raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a loom weaves cloth

explanation.surface: Continuing a run of clues, this one pictures a weaving frame being hoisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this to 16-down, where QUID was money; 'more of the same' means another word for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is slang for cash, so it supplies yet another money word after the quid in the linked clue.

clue.text: Closes in on prey, after antelope

indicators.note: the closes of words are their endings, so only final letters are taken

parts.note: the last letter of in
the last letter of prey
à la means after the manner of

explanation.surface: A predator closes on its quarry while hunting an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closes in on' reads as one phrase for a hunter approaching, but 'closes' alone takes the ends of 'in' and 'prey'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope with a shaggy coat, a species within that family of grazers.

clue.text: College beak looking over hopeful's entry form

indicators.note: looking over one's shoulder means facing backwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: neb is a dialect word for a bird's beak
C is an abbreviation for college

indicators.note: the entry is where one comes in, the very start, so the first letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of hopeful

explanation.surface: A college magistrate checks over an applicant's admission paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' and 'form' suggest a judge and paperwork; here a beak is a bird's bill, and a form is a long wooden seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a long backless seat, as in old schoolrooms, and a bench is the same sort of furniture.

clue.text: Reported guy seen on canal side?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: a bargee is a man who works a canal barge

explanation.surface: A rumour of a man spotted on a towpath beside the canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like the bank of the canal; it is a side dish. A bhaji is a spiced fried vegetable fritter served at Indian restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion bhajis are commonly ordered as an accompanying dish with an Indian meal, so the fritter is a side order.

clue.text: I'll give wry renditions no end

definitions.text: I'll give wry renditions no end

indicators.note: wry means twisted or bent out of shape, so the letters are turned into a new order
with no end means the word end is removed from what comes before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be taken away

explanation.surface: A speaker boasts of endlessly delivering sardonic performances.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove END from RENDITIONS and twist what remains; read whole, the clue is the speaker's own boast.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironist habitually says the opposite of what is meant, a mocking sardonic style, which is constant wryness.

clue.text: A bewitching old woman keeps back ingredient

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the words before it are each read from the end

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means alluring or bewitching
ma is a familiar name for one's mother

explanation.surface: A witch-like old woman holds on to one of her potion components.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend, and Chambers also gives it the older sense of a single component in a mixture.

clue.text: Canary with the cuckoo flower

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are scrambled into madness

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Two songbirds, a canary and a cuckoo, sit side by side among the blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The water hyacinth is a floating tropical aquatic plant with showy mauve blooms, so it is one kind of flowering plant.
